R["eee The use of estrogen, progesterone, or selective ER modulators to treat osteoporosis or osteopenia in patients with breast cancer is discouraged. The use of a bisphosphonate (oral/IV) or denosumab is acceptable to maintain or to improve BMD and reduce risk of fractures in postmenopausal (natural or induced) patients receiving adjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy. Optimal duration of either therapy has not been established. Benefits of duration beyond 3 years or optimal duration beyond 3 years is not known. Breast Cancer During Pregnancy"] --> N02["GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS FOR MANAGEMENT OF BREAST CANCER DURING PREGNANCY¹⁻³"]
    N02 --> N03["General Considerations
• Considerations and selection of optimal local therapy and systemic therapy are similar to that recommended in non–pregnancy-associated breast cancer.
• The selection and timing of chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and RT are different for pregnancy-associated breast cancer compared to non–pregnancy-associated breast cancer.
• BCS during the first trimester of pregnancy can be considered in those who will require adjuvant chemotherapy and can have adjuvant RT delayed until after delivery.
• Chemotherapy should not be administered during the first trimester of pregnancy.
• RT should not be administered during any trimester of pregnancy.
• Coordination is recommended between the oncology and obstetrics teams to plan the optimal timing of systemic therapy administration during pregnancy.
• Considerations for postpartum chemotherapy are the same as for non–pregnancy-associated breast cancer."]
    N03 --> N04["Considerations for Systemic Therapy
• A fetal examination with ultrasound should be performed prior to systemic therapy administration to exclude pre-existing abnormalities.
• Standard-dose chemotherapy should be used based on actual weight.
• Anthracycline, cyclophosphamide, and taxanes appear to be safe during the second and third trimesters.
  ▸ Doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide every 3 weeks is preferred. Limited data suggest that dd AC with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) use during pregnancy appears to be safe.
  ▸ Weekly paclitaxel is preferred.
• Avoid chemotherapy after 35 weeks to allow maternal bone marrow to recover before the delivery.
• The following agents are contraindicated:
  ▸ Anti-HER2 therapies: trastuzumab, pertuzumab, ado-trastuzumab emtansine, fam-trastuzumab-deruxtecan-nxki, neratinib, lapatinib, tucatinib
  ▸ CDK4/6 inhibitors (there are no data on safety)
  ▸ Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs): fam trastuzumab-deruxtecan-nxki, datopotamab deruxtecan-dlnk, sacituzumab govitecan-hziy
  ▸ Endocrine therapy: tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitor, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists/antagonists
  ▸ PARP inhibitors
  ▸ Immune checkpoint inhibitors"]

• Antiemetics: Ondansetron and metoclopramide are considered safe.
• NK1 inhibitors: Avoid using these, as data from human studies are lacking.
• Steroids:
  ▸ Methylprednisolone, prednisolone, or hydrocortisone are preferred.
  ▸ Avoid dexamethasone or betamethasone if possible.
• G-CSF: Use with caution. There are insufficient data to support G-CSF use, but it appears to be safe during pregnancy."]
